info.name: GoHighLevel API (Campground POS Integration)
info.description:
# GoHighLevel API — Campground POS Integration

Every real GoHighLevel (Lead Connector) endpoint this app's backend calls, extracted directly from `campground-backend`'s `App\Integrations\GHL\GhlClient` and `App\Services\Ghl*` classes — not inferred from GHL's public docs alone, so every gotcha noted here (required-vs-rejected fields, which Version header, which base URL) reflects what this integration has confirmed live against a real GHL account.

This is a companion to the **Campground POS API** collection, which covers this app's OWN backend routes. Use *that* collection to drive the app; use *this* one to poke at GoHighLevel directly — e.g. to debug why a sync failed, or to see exactly what a "Pull Data Service" click actually sends.

## Setup
1. Run **0. OAuth** to get a real `access_token`/`refresh_token` for a location — or, faster, copy them from an already-connected location: `campground-backend`'s `engage_tokens` table, or ask this app for its `location_id` via `GET /superadmin/engage-identifiers` (in the Campground POS API collection) and the access token from wherever your OAuth app stores it.
2. Set `access_token` and `location_id` in this collection's variables (or the companion environment file). Collection-level auth is Bearer `{{access_token}}`, applied to every request automatically.
3. Fill in `contact_id`/`product_id`/`service_id`/etc. as you create real records, or copy real ids from a GET response.

## Base URLs — two, not one
Almost everything is `{{ghl_services_base_url}}` (`https://services.leadconnectorhq.com`). Two endpoints in **9. Calendars — Bookings** are on `{{ghl_backend_base_url}}` (`https://backend.leadconnectorhq.com`) instead — GHL's calendar-booking creation flow lives on a different host entirely. Confirmed live in `GhlClient::postToBackend()`.

## Version headers vary by endpoint — read each request's description
GHL's API versioning isn't uniform: most endpoints use your connection's default (`2021-07-28`), **calendars/service-categories** requires `v3` specifically (401s under other versions even with a fully-scoped token), **calendars/services/bookings/{id}** requires `2021-04-15` specifically, and **invoices/** (list) requires `v3` while most other invoice endpoints use `2021-07-28`. Every request below carries the exact Version header this app actually sends.

## altId/altType vs locationId — also endpoint-specific
GET requests mostly use `locationId` as a query param; POST/PUT bodies mostly use `altId`+`altType` instead (GHL's newer convention). A few endpoints want both, or reject one where you'd expect it (e.g. Update Contact rejects `locationId`; Update Service Category rejects it too, but Create Service Category *requires* it). Each request's description calls out the specific rule, confirmed live rather than guessed.

variable.value: contacts.readonly contacts.write products.readonly products.write products%2Fprices.readonly products%2Fprices.write products%2Fcollection.readonly products%2Fcollection.write invoices.readonly invoices.write invoices%2Fschedule.readonly invoices%2Fschedule.write calendars.readonly calendars.write calendars%2Fevents.readonly calendars%2Fevents.write calendars%2Fresources.readonly calendars%2Fgroups.readonly

item.name: 0. OAuth (Authorization Code + Refresh)
1. Authorize URL (open in browser, not a Postman call)

request.description:
Not a real Postman request — GHL's OAuth authorize screen is a browser page, not a JSON API. Open this URL in a real browser, approve the requested scopes for a location, and GHL redirects back to your app's redirect_uri with a `code` query param. Paste that code into the `auth_code` variable and run the next request.

Mirrors App\Services\GhlAuthService::getAuthorizationUrl() in campground-backend — `scope` is a space-separated list (GhlAuthService::DEFAULT_SCOPES), `state` carries this app's organization id so the callback knows which org's token row to update.

Form-encoded, NOT JSON — GHL's token endpoint rejects a JSON body. Response contains access_token/refresh_token/expires_in/locationId/userId/companyId; save access_token into the `access_token` variable (collection auth uses it) and refresh_token into `refresh_token`.

Mirrors GhlAuthService::exchangeCodeForTokens()/exchangeCodeForTokensWithoutOrganization().

GHL's refresh_token is one-time-use/rotating — always save the NEW refresh_token from the response back into the `refresh_token` variable, or the next refresh will fail. Same endpoint/shape as token exchange, different grant_type.

Mirrors GhlAuthService::refreshAccessToken().

item.description: GHL's OAuth2 flow. Every other folder below needs `access_token`/`location_id` populated first — either run this flow for real, or copy an already-authorized location's values from this app's own /admin/engages/tokens page (owner/admin) or /superadmin/engage-identifiers (super-admin).

item.name: 1. Contacts

request.description:
Paginated (page/limit). Used by GhlService::bulkPullContacts() for the "Pull Data Service" contacts phase — same query shape.

Roles this app maps a GHL contact onto: engage_customers (global, deduped by email/phone) + engage_customers_locations (per-location link carrying ghl_contact_id).

locationId is REQUIRED in the body on create (unlike PUT, see below). A 400 with a `contactId` in the error body means a contact with this email/phone already exists — extract it and treat as the existing contact rather than retrying (this app's GhlService::syncContactToGhl() does exactly that).

Mirrors GhlService::syncContactToGhl()'s create branch.

Do NOT send `locationId` in this body — GHL's PUT rejects it (a real gotcha this app's GhlService::syncContactToGhl() comment calls out explicitly: "PUT does not accept locationId").

Mirrors GhlService::syncContactToGhl()'s update branch.
Mirrors GhlService::deleteContactFromGhl() — this app treats the result as non-blocking (failures logged, local delete proceeds regardless).

item.description: GHL's Contacts API — the CRM record this app syncs its own engage_customers rows to/from.

item.name: 2. Opportunities

request.description:
Created alongside every booking (non-blocking — failure never stops the booking itself). `status` values this app sends: new/booked/lost, per the POS status <-> GHL stage mapping in CLAUDE.md.

Mirrors GhlService::createOpportunity().
Mirrors GhlService::updateOpportunityStage() — fired when a booking's local status changes (pending->confirmed maps to new->booked, cancelled maps to lost).

item.description: One opportunity is created per booking for pipeline visibility in GHL; kept loosely in sync with the booking's local status.

item.name: 3. Products (Payments Products API)

request.description: Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::fetchAllGhlProducts() (used by "Pull All from GHL"). Paginate via offset until a page returns fewer than `limit` rows.
Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::pullFromGhl() — response's `collectionIds` array is what this app reads back onto its local product_categories pivot (see CLAUDE.md's Category Tab fix).

productType: PHYSICAL | DIGITAL | SERVICE. isTaxesEnabled MUST be false unless a non-empty `taxes` array of real GHL tax-category ids is also sent (this app never sends true — see GhlProductSyncService's doc comment: sending true without taxes throws a live 422 "taxes should not be empty").

For a variable product, also send `isVariable: true` plus a `variants` array (each variant needs `id`+`name`; each option needs `id`+`name` as objects, not strings) — see GHL API quirks in CLAUDE.md.

Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncProductToGhl()'s create branch.

body.raw:
{
  "altId": "{{location_id}}",
  "altType": "location",
  "locationId": "{{location_id}}",
  "name": "Firewood Bundle",
  "description": "A bundle of seasoned firewood, ready to burn.",
  "productType": "PHYSICAL",
  "status": "active",
  "availableInStore": true,
  "isTaxesEnabled": false,
  "taxInclusive": false,
  "trackProductInventory": true,
  "slug": "firewood-bundle",
  "collectionIds": [
    "{{collection_id}}"
  ]
}

request.description:
If this product has variants, always re-send the SAME `ghl_variant_id` GHL assigned on a prior create — sending a placeholder/local id instead makes GHL rebuild the whole variant structure and hides the Variants/Pricing tabs in the GHL UI (a real, previously-hit bug documented in CLAUDE.md).

Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncProductToGhl()'s update branch.

body.raw:
{
  "altId": "{{location_id}}",
  "altType": "location",
  "locationId": "{{location_id}}",
  "name": "Firewood Bundle",
  "description": "A bundle of seasoned firewood, ready to burn.",
  "productType": "PHYSICAL",
  "status": "active",
  "availableInStore": true,
  "isTaxesEnabled": false,
  "taxInclusive": false,
  "trackProductInventory": true
}

request.description: Mirrors GhlProductSyncService (used when a synced local product is deleted).

item.description: GHL's regular catalog (Payments Products) API — for standalone POS goods, not rental listings (those live under Calendars/Services, folder 7).

item.name: 4. Product Prices & Inventory

request.description:
A GHL Price object carries trackInventory/availableQuantity/allowOutOfStockPurchases alongside the price itself — one call covers both live price and live stock. The DEFAULT price is the one with an empty/absent `variantOptionIds` array.

Mirrors GhlProductGateway::fetchLive() (Product Sales page's live stock check) and GhlProductSyncService::pullDefaultPriceFromGhl().

For a variant price, also send `variantOptionIds: ["{{ghl_option_id}}"]` to link the price to a specific variant option.

Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncDefaultPriceToGhl()'s create branch — only fires when no default price exists yet (find-or-create prevents duplicates).
Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncDefaultPriceToGhl()'s update branch — PUT if engage_price_id/an existing default price is already known, to avoid creating a duplicate price.

GHL sets an ABSOLUTE quantity here, not a decrement — there is no atomic "reduce stock by N" endpoint. Callers must read the current quantity first (List Prices above) and compute the new value themselves before calling this.

Mirrors GhlProductGateway::updateInventory(), called right after a POS product sale decrements local stock.

item.description: Pricing and live stock for regular catalog products (folder 3). `items` supports multiple price ids per call even though this app only ever sends one at a time.

item.name: 5. Product Collections (Categories)

request.description: Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::fetchAllGhlCollections() — used by both the category pull and the outbound name-match-before-create dedup check.

Unlike calendars/service-categories (folder 8), GHL derives nothing automatically here either — always send both `name` and `slug`.

Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncCategoryToGhl()'s create branch.
Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::syncCategoryToGhl()'s update branch.
Mirrors GhlProductSyncService::deleteCategoryFromGhl().

item.description: Product Categories in this app's own admin UI map onto GHL "Collections" — a regular-catalog-only concept, distinct from calendars/service-categories (folder 8), which is the rental-only equivalent.

item.name: 6. Media

request.description:
multipart/form-data, NOT JSON — select a real image file for the `file` field in Postman before sending (can't be pre-filled). Response shape: `{"uploadedFiles": {"<filename>": "https://cdn..."}}` — the returned CDN URL is what gets cached locally (ghl_image_url) and sent as a product/category's `image` field.

Mirrors GhlClient::uploadFile(), used by GhlImageSyncService for local-to-GHL image push.

item.description: GHL's media library — used to push a locally-uploaded product/category image to GHL's CDN before referencing it on a product/collection payload.

item.name: 7. Calendars — Rentals (Services)

request.description:
NOT calendars/services/catalog — that's classic Services v2 and is often empty for rental accounts (a real gotcha documented throughout this app's CLAUDE.md). Returns BOTH base listings and their variants as flat entries, each carrying its own `productId` (the payments-layer product backing that specific service/variant).

Mirrors GhlServiceSyncService::pullServices()/fetchRentalProductIds().

The single source of truth for a rental's live pricing rules, durations, availability, and quantity — this app fetches this on demand and caches it 5 minutes, NEVER persists it to its own database (see GhlRentalGateway's doc comment / CLAUDE.md's "Rental detail is not in the database" convention).

Mirrors GhlRentalGateway::fetchServiceDetail()/fetchListingBundle().

item.description: GHL Calendar "rental" industry-type services — this app's entire rental/booking catalog lives here, not in the Payments Products API (folder 3).

item.name: 8. Calendars — Rental Service Categories

request.description:
The rental-only equivalent of products/collections (folder 5) — a completely separate GHL concept from regular-catalog Collections. Version header MUST be v3.

Mirrors GhlServiceSyncService::pullServiceCategories().

Three confirmed-live gotchas (see GhlServiceSyncService::syncServiceCategoryToGhl()'s doc comment — found by testing both verbs for real, not guessed):
1. `industryType=rental` must be a QUERY param on every write call (POST/PUT/DELETE), not just GET.
2. POST requires `locationId` in the body (422 "locationId can't be undefined" without it).
3. Both POST and PUT require `slug` in the body — GHL does NOT derive one from `name` automatically here (unlike products/collections).

Response nests the created record under a `serviceCategory` key: `{"serviceCategory": {"_id": ...}}`, not top-level.
PUT REJECTS `locationId` in the body (422 "property locationId should not exist") — the exact opposite of POST's requirement. Easy to miss without testing both verbs for real.

Needs `industryType` as a query param too — not `altId`/`altType`/`locationId` the way products/collections' DELETE does.

Mirrors GhlServiceSyncService::deleteServiceCategoryFromGhl().

item.description: Version header must be v3 for every request in this folder — confirmed live, GHL 401s these endpoints under other Version values even with a fully-scoped token.

item.name: 9. Calendars — Bookings

request.description:
Step 1 of creating a real rental booking. Note the base URL is backend.leadconnectorhq.com, NOT services.leadconnectorhq.com like every other request in this collection — GHL's calendar-booking creation flow lives on a different host entirely.

`id` is the rental's PAYMENTS product id (GhlServiceDetail::paymentsProductId()), not the calendar service id.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::createBooking()'s first call.

Step 2 — auto-generates a GHL invoice as a side effect (extract its id from the response to drive Send Invoice / Record Payment below). Also on backend.leadconnectorhq.com, same as the fees call above.

The `selectedSlotInfo.services[0]` shape here is simplified for manual testing — this app's real payload (GhlBookingService::buildSelectedService()) includes GHL's live pricing-rule breakdown fields too; the minimal shape above is what's actually required to create a booking.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::createBooking()'s second call.

Version header MUST be 2021-04-15 (GhlClient::BOOKING_API_VERSION) — this is the one endpoint in the whole integration pinned to that specific version. Status values this app sends: new | confirmed.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::updateBookingStatus().

Same pinned Version as Update Booking Status. Called when a local booking is cancelled; this app also voids the linked invoice separately afterward (see Void Invoice below) so the payment link stops accepting payment.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::cancelBooking().

item.description: Creating/updating a real GHL Calendar rental booking. The two "create" steps run on a DIFFERENT base URL (backend.leadconnectorhq.com) than everything else in this collection.

item.name: 10. Invoices

request.description:
`status=paid` is a real, documented server-side filter (confirmed against GHL's own List Invoices reference) — used by the full-sync "reconcile paid invoices" phase to pull only already-paid invoices rather than fetching everything and filtering client-side.

Mirrors GhlFullSyncService's paid-invoices phase.

Used by this app's self-healing invoice-status reconciliation (GhlService::reconcileInvoiceStatus()) — never used to render "the invoice" itself anymore (that's now rendered from local snapshotted data, see InvoiceService in CLAUDE.md), only to check/sync payment status.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::syncInvoiceMetadata().

A standalone payment-link invoice with no calendar slot attached — used for staff "Online"/card bookings and POS product sales, not the auto-generated invoice from Create Booking above. `action`: "send" emails the customer a real payment link; "draft" creates it silently (used for an already-paid-in-person cash POS sale, which then immediately calls Record Payment below).

`liveMode: false` matches this GHL location's connected payment processor in dev — flip to true only once a live Stripe/NMI account is connected, or checkout fails with "No valid payment method available" (a real gotcha called out in GhlBookingService's own doc comment).

Optionally add `businessDetails: {name, logoUrl, phoneNo}` to brand the hosted invoice page with your own logo instead of GHL's default (logoUrl must be a fully-qualified URL).

Mirrors GhlBookingService::createText2PayInvoice()/createProductSaleInvoice().

Emails the customer the invoice's existing payment link — used after Create Booking (folder 9) auto-generates an invoice, since that endpoint doesn't email it itself.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::sendInvoice().

`mode`: cash | card | other. Called when staff marks a booking/sale paid in the POS, or when a guest's Text2Pay invoice is confirmed paid via webhook/reconciliation.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::recordInvoicePayment()/recordProductSaleInvoicePayment().

Stops an unpaid invoice's payment link from accepting payment — called when a booking is cancelled while its invoice is still unpaid.

Mirrors GhlBookingService::voidInvoice().

item.description: GHL's Invoices API — every payment link, payment recording, and paid-status check in this app goes through here. Note the mixed Version headers: v3 for List Invoices, 2021-07-28 for text2pay/send/void, and no explicit version (falls back to your connection's default) for Get Invoice/Record Payment.
